description: Bound the built-in otel.db store by a 72h retention age and a 1 GiB (db+WAL+SHM) size budget with online reclamation, a write-admission backstop, and startup recovery for oversized databases.

tasks.title: Time-based trace retention
tasks.description: Add RetentionMaxAge (default 72h) to OtelOptions and implement an IOtelMaintenanceCallback registered in DI that, on each enabled 10s tick and the first post-start probe, deletes complete Traces (the Trace header row plus every Span row sharing its trace_id in one transaction) whose end_time is older than now - RetentionMaxAge. Deletion runs oldest-first in bounded batches and resumes on the next tick if interrupted. Add an idx_traces_end index on traces(end_time) to OtelDb.EnsureInitialized (and mirror it in the InMemoryOtelDb test helper) so the end_time-based retention deletion is index-served rather than a table scan. All time logic uses the injected TimeProvider; the callback runs only while observation is enabled.
acceptanceCriteria: RetentionMaxAge is bound from Mohist:Otel and defaults to 72h with no additional user-tunable retention knobs.

After FakeTimeProvider advances past RetentionMaxAge without wall-clock elapsing, the next maintenance pass deletes each aged Trace's header row and all of its Span rows, leaving no orphan Trace or Span rows.
When aged Traces exceed the batch size, one pass deletes at most one batch and subsequent passes remove the remainder oldest-first without duplicating or skipping work.
A cancelled mid-pass leaves committed deletions in place and the next pass resumes from the oldest remaining aged Trace.
While observation is disabled, the maintenance loop does not run and no Trace or Span is deleted; re-enabling resumes from the current injected time without deleting in-window Traces.

An idx_traces_end index on traces(end_time) is created at schema init; the retention deletion filters via this index and per-pass database statement count stays proportional to the batch size and does not grow with unrelated history, asserted via operation counts with no COUNT(*) over the Trace or Span tables.
tasks.output: RetentionMaxAge config, the retention IOtelMaintenanceCallback with bounded complete-Trace deletion, DI registration, and passing spec/unit tests using FakeTimeProvider + InMemoryOtelDb.
tasks.notes: Introduces the IOtelMaintenanceCallback registration that T-002 extends, and the idx_traces_end index that T-002's EnsureInitialized changes build on. Does not touch auto_vacuum or size eviction.

tasks.title: Hard size budget with ingest admission backstop
tasks.description: Add StorageBudgetBytes (default 1 GiB, from RuntimeValueRules.StorageBudgetBytes) to OtelOptions. Enable auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL in OtelDb.EnsureInitialized before table creation and add bounded incremental_vacuum($pages) plus wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) reclaim helpers. Extend the maintenance callback with size eviction: while the storage probe reports combined db+WAL+SHM usage at/above the 90% high watermark, delete oldest complete Traces by start_time until usage drops below the 80% low watermark or no removable Trace remains; then reclaim and re-probe, yielding (no busy-wait) when the truncating checkpoint is blocked. Introduce a singleton OtelStorageGuard holding admission-closed state and persisting a minimal reclamation/admission marker to a local .meta sidecar (via IFileSystem) after each arbitration; on startup the guard seeds admission from the marker, and a missing or corrupt marker falls back to admission-closed until the first probe re-derives the watermark (so correctness never depends on the marker). The guard closes admission when reclamation cannot keep up and reopens it once usage is below the low watermark. Add a budget-aware IIngestProtectionDecision that replaces AcceptAllIngestProtectionDecision, rejecting every Span while admission is closed so rejections flow through the existing RecordIngest path to OTLP partial_success with a non-retry instruction. Add the storage_budget_exhausted degradation code on the IngestProtection source, published/cleared under the shared state lock. This task delivers both the otel-storage-budget and otel-ingest-admission capabilities because the guard, the eviction signal, and the write-path call-site switchover are one tightly-coupled feature module.
acceptanceCriteria: StorageBudgetBytes is bound from Mohist:Otel, defaults to 1 GiB, and leaves the budget value reported by /otel/api/status unchanged.
Fresh otel.db files are created with auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL; the online maintenance path issues incremental_vacuum and wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and a test locks that no full VACUUM is ever issued.
With a fake IOtelStorageProbe reporting usage at/above 90%, the callback deletes oldest complete Traces and stops once the fake reports below 80%; below 80% it performs no eviction.

When reclamation cannot reduce usage below 80% (no removable Trace, or a blocked checkpoint), admission closes, an attempted write is refused promptly, and OTLP partial_success reports the rejected Span count without the sender retrying.

The guard persists a minimal reclamation/admission marker to a local .meta sidecar via IFileSystem and seeds admission from it on startup; a missing or corrupt marker falls back to admission-closed until the first probe re-derives the watermark, so a restart into an over-budget store never accepts writes as healthy regardless of marker state.

While writes are refused, /otel/api/status and mo otel status report degraded with a storage_budget_exhausted latest_degradation reason (published/cleared under the state lock so it dominates while admission is closed) that clears when reclamation recovers, leaving the off/healthy/degraded tri-state contract intact.
Admission refusal completes without blocking and does not delay the request thread, Workflow scheduler, or Runner communication, asserted without wall-clock waits.
Eviction and reclamation cost per tick is bounded and independent of unrelated history, asserted via operation counts.
tasks.output: StorageBudgetBytes config, auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL init, incremental_vacuum/wal_checkpoint reclaim helpers, size-eviction + reclaim in the maintenance callback, OtelStorageGuard, budget-aware IIngestProtectionDecision, storage_budget_exhausted degradation code, and passing spec/unit tests using a fake IOtelStorageProbe, InMemoryOtelDb, and FakeTimeProvider.
tasks.notes: Extends the maintenance callback introduced in T-001. Realizes specs/otel-storage-budget/spec.md and specs/otel-ingest-admission/spec.md together; the guard is the shared state both eviction and admission depend on, so they ship as one feature module.

tasks.title: Startup recovery for an oversized observation database
tasks.description: On the maintenance loop's first post-start tick, if the storage probe reports combined db+WAL+SHM usage above 100% of StorageBudgetBytes (strictly above the 90% eviction high watermark, so eviction gets the first chance to reclaim), rebuild an empty observation database: clear the SQLite connection pool for the old file, delete the old db/wal/shm (and the .meta sidecar) through IFileSystem, and let OtelDb.EnsureInitialized recreate a fresh schema with auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL. Emit one structured observation-data-reset log and publish the storage_data_reset degradation code on the StorageWrite source (added to RuntimeDegradationCodes.IsValidFor), cleared by the first committed production write. A read-only query overlapping the bounded rebuild window fails and surfaces through the existing storage-read degradation path rather than blocking or corrupting the rebuild. Detection and rebuild are bounded (file-length reads plus pool clear; no Trace/Span scan), run off the core startup path, and a rebuild failure is contained to observation without affecting core reachability or the business database.
acceptanceCriteria: With a fake probe reporting usage above 100% of StorageBudgetBytes at startup, recovery clears the connection pool, removes the old db/wal/shm and .meta files via a fake IFileSystem, and initializes a fresh empty database with auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL.
With usage at or below the budget at startup, no rebuild occurs and existing observation data is preserved.

The rebuild emits exactly one structured data-reset log and publishes the storage_data_reset degradation code on the StorageWrite source, visible in /otel/api/status and mo otel status; the code clears after the first new committed production write and the next observation runs with no other active cause.
A read-only observation query overlapping the bounded rebuild window fails and surfaces through the existing storage-read degradation path without blocking or corrupting the rebuild.
Rebuild detection and connection-clearing cost is bounded and does not scan or iterate Traces or Spans, asserted once with little and once with much history yielding equal bounded work.
A rebuild failure leaves the store unusable for observation but does not prevent the core Server from becoming reachable, and never touches or locks the business database; /api/health is unaffected.
tasks.output: Startup recovery path on the maintenance first-tick, storage_data_reset degradation code and log, and passing spec/unit tests using a fake IOtelStorageProbe, fake IFileSystem, and connection-pool seam.
tasks.notes: Uses the StorageBudgetBytes threshold and the maintenance first-tick from T-001/T-002. Depends transitively on T-001 via T-002.
